གསུངས་པ་ཡི། །ཐུབ་དབང་དེ་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། །གང་གིས་བློ་གྲོས་#ཡོད་མེད་ལས། །རྣམ་པར་འདས་ཤིང་མི་གནས་པ། །དེ་དག་གིས་ནི་རྐྱེན་གྱི་དོན། །ཟབ་མོ་དམིགས་མེད་རྣམ་པར་རྟོགས། །རེ་ཞིག་ཉེས་ཀུན་འབྱུང་བའི་གནས། །མེད་ཉིད་རྣམ་པར་བཟློག་ཟིན་གྱིས། །རིགས་#

སུ་ཤེས་པས་མིན། །དེ་ནི་སུ་ལ་མངོན་སུམ་འགྱུར། །ཞིག་ཤེས་པ་དེར་ཇི་ལྟར་འགྱུར། །གལ་ཏེ་ཕུང་པོ་མ་འགགས་ན། །ཉོན་མོངས་ཟད་ཀྱང་འདས་མི་འགྱུར། །གང་ཚེ་འདིར་ནི་འགགས་གྱུར་པ། །དེ་ཡི་ཚེ་ན་གྲོལ་བར་འགྱུར། །མ་རིག་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་བྱུང་བ་ལ། །ཡང་དག་ཡེ་ཤེས་
ཀྱིས་གཟིགས་ནས#། །སྐྱེ་བ་དང་ནི་འགགས་པའང་རུང་། །འགའ་ཡང་དམིགས་པར་མི་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེ་ཉིད་མཐོང་ཆོས་མྱ་ངན་#འདས། །འདས་ཤིང་བྱ་བ་བྱས་པའང་ཡིན། །གལ་ཏེ་ཆོས་ཤེས་མཇུག་#ཐོགས་སུ། །འདི་ལ་བྱེ་བྲག་ཡོད་ན་ནི། །དངོས་པོ་ཤིན་ཏུ་ཕྲ་བ་ལའང་། །གང་
span:
In the language of India: <term>Yuktiṣaṣṭikākārikā-nāma</term> <gloss>The Sixty Stanzas on Reasoning</gloss>.
In the language of Tibet: <term>Rigs pa drug cu pa'i tshig le'ur byas pa zhes bya ba</term>.
Homage to Manjushri, the Youthful.

I prostrate to the King of Sages <note>the Buddha</note>,
Who taught dependent origination,
The method by which
Birth and destruction are abandoned.

Those whose minds have transcended
Existence and non-existence, and who do not remain in them,
Realize the profound meaning of conditionality,
Which is free from any focal point.

Since the state of non-existence, the source of all faults,
Has already been turned away,
Listen now to how the state of existence
Is turned away through reasoning.

If things were true
In the way that children imagine them,
Why would one not desire liberation
Since those things would then be non-existent? <note>Implying that if things had inherent existence, their cessation would be total annihilation, which is not what liberation means.</note>

One is not liberated through existence,
Nor from this cyclic existence through non-existence.
By thoroughly knowing existence and non-existence,
The Great Beings are liberated.

Those who do not see suchness
Conceive of the world and <term>nirvana</term> <gloss>liberation from suffering</gloss>;
Those who see suchness
Do not conceive of the world and nirvana.

Existence and nirvana
Neither of these two exists.
The thorough knowledge of existence itself
Is what is called nirvana.

Just as the cessation of a thing
Is imagined when it has arisen and then perished,
So too do the Sublime Ones
Accept cessation like a magical illusion.

Cessation occurs through thorough knowledge of the conditioned,
Not through a process of destruction.
To whom would that be manifest?
How could there be knowledge of what has perished?

If the <term>skandhas</term> <gloss>aggregates of body and mind</gloss> did not cease,
One would not transcend even if afflictions were exhausted.
When they have ceased here in this very life,
At that time one becomes liberated.

When one sees with perfect wisdom
What arises through the condition of ignorance,
Neither arising
Nor even cessation can be perceived.

That is nirvana seen in this very life,
The task is accomplished and done.
If there were any distinction in this
Following the knowledge of phenomena,

One who imagines birth
Even in the most subtle of things,
Is unwise and
Has not seen the meaning of what arises from conditions.

In Indian language: <term>Yuktisastika-karika-nama</term>. 
In Tibetan language: <term>Rigs pa drug cu pa'i tshig le'ur byas pa zhes bya ba</term> <gloss>Sixty Verses on Reasoning</gloss>.

Prostration to Manjushri the Youthful.

I prostrate to the Prince of Sages, who taught dependent origination, by which method arising and perishing are abandoned.

Those whose minds have transcended "existence" and "non-existence" and do not dwell there, they realize the profound, objectless meaning of conditions. 

First, the position of "non-existence," which is the source of all faults, has been averted. Now, listen to the reasoning by which "existence" itself is also averted. 

If things were true in the way they are conceptualized by children <note>spiritually immature people</note>, why would one not desire liberation through the non-existence of those things?

One is not liberated through "existence," and one is not freed from this becoming through "non-existence." Through thoroughly knowing "thing" and "non-thing," the great-souled ones are liberated.

Those who do not see reality think in terms of "the world" and "nirvana." Those who see reality do not think in terms of "the world" and "nirvana." 

Becoming and nirvana—these two do not exist. The thorough knowledge of becoming itself is called nirvana. 

Just as the cessation of a produced thing is conceptualized as "extinction," likewise the Noble Ones accept cessation to be like a magical illusion. 

Cessation occurs through the thorough knowledge of the conditioned, not through its destruction. To whom would that be manifest? How could there be a knowledge of destruction there?

If the aggregates have not ceased, even if the afflictions are exhausted, one has not passed beyond <note>suffering</note>. When they are ceased here, at that time one is liberated.

Regarding that which arises through the condition of ignorance, having seen it with perfect gnosis, one does not perceive any arising or even any ceasing. 

This is nirvana in this very life; it is to have passed beyond and to have done what was to be done. If there were a distinction in this after knowing the Dharma, even regarding the most subtle thing, then...
